description: Window cleaning in Lakewind Estates, 55 hilltop homes with Lake Travis views. Pure water poles, about $0.10 per sq ft, quotes from Tyler by text.
intro: Lakewind Estates is a gated hilltop community of 55 homes with Lake Travis views, set on lots of one to seven acres. CleanzATX cleans the tall view windows here with pure water poles, and Tyler Durham quotes each home himself.

sections.h2: What Lakewind Estates homes are like
paragraphs: Toll Brothers built this community in the early 2000s, and 55 homes share a gated hilltop. Lots run from one to seven acres, homes are 3,500 to 6,000 sq ft, and prices range from $1.2M to $2.5M. The Lakewind Estates HOA manages the community.

After more than two decades the homes have settled in. Landscaping has grown up, trees have filled in around patios, and the original stucco and stone have weathered. Many owners now repaint, redo outdoor spaces or refresh the exteriors, and clean windows are often the first thing they notice afterward.

sections.h2: What Lakewind Estates windows deal with
paragraphs: A hilltop is exposed. Wind carries dust and pollen up the slope, and the view windows that make the homes special are also the largest panes in the house. Glass facing the lake takes direct afternoon sun, and streaks that are invisible in the morning show up strongly after lunch. Pure water, with water near 0 TDS, dries without spots or a soap film.

With acreage comes sprinkler coverage, so lower windows often show mineral spotting from irrigation. Trees on the property bring webs and leaf litter to screens and tracks, and older stucco holds green growth on shaded walls. We remove hard water at $10 per pane.

The community is gated, so give us the code or a contact when you book. The drives are long and the slopes can be steep, which is where water fed poles help: we reach up to three stories from the ground, without ladders on uneven ground. We plan the visit by side of the house so we can work with the sun, and we usually pair windows with a soft wash on stucco and stone.
For a 4,500 sq ft home, exterior windows come to about $450 at $0.10 per sq ft. Expect roughly three and a half to four and a half hours on site for the outside, and about half that for the inside.

faq.q: Do you work in gated communities with long driveways?
faq.a: Yes. Send us the code or the contact name with your request. Long drives are fine, and we work from the truck or move equipment up to the house as needed.

faq.q: Why do my big view windows show streaks in the afternoon?
faq.a: Afternoon sun hits lake facing glass directly, and any residue from soap or tap water catches that light. Pure water leaves almost nothing behind, so the glass dries clear and stays clearer between visits.

faq.q: Can you reach the upper windows on a three story front?
faq.a: Yes. Water fed poles reach up to three stories from the ground. Some window designs, such as stair towers, may need a closer look, and we will say so in the quote.

faq.q: What is the price for a home in the 3,500 to 6,000 sq ft range?
faq.a: At about $0.10 per sq ft, exterior windows run roughly $350 to $600. You can also go by $10 per window. Inside and out is $15 per window. Quotes by text take about an hour in business hours.

faq.q: Can you also wash stucco and stone?
faq.a: Yes, with a soft wash system at low pressure. House soft wash starts at $0.20 per sq ft with a $400 minimum. We never pressure wash limestone, and we adjust the method for stucco, stone or painted siding.
